one_month_reasoning: AMD's own Q3 2026 report is expected ~Nov 3 after the close (unconfirmed per earnings calendars), i.e. just OUTSIDE the Oct 30 window, so the stock's biggest scheduled event does not resolve inside it. Inside the window: TSMC Q3 results/monthly sales (mid-Oct), and the late-October hyperscaler prints (Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet, Amazon ~Oct 27-30) whose 2027 capex guides are the key read-through for Helios/MI450 demand; pre-earnings positioning into Nov 3 and first Helios customer-rack shipment chatter (racks were slated to ship from late Q3). The stock just made an ATH at $639 (Sep 25), pulled back to ~$600 support in a semis selloff, then bounced on the World Labs deal. Momentum is strong but the move is extended; I see no clear directional edge, so I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred at ~$606 (tiny positive drift for momentum/pre-earnings run-up) with sigma 0.19, slightly below the 72%/3.5 = 20.6% rule because the dominant event (earnings) falls just after the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (70%): ~$20 2028E EPS (as the market will price it in Sep 2027) x 30x on ~1.70B diluted shares = $600; and EV/NTM sales (30%): ~$90B NTM revenue x 10x plus ~$15B net cash over 1.70B shares = $540. Blended ~$582, roughly at today's price.

base.story: Helios ships from late Q3 2026 and ramps through 2027 with OpenAI, Meta, Oracle, Anthropic; DC roughly doubles, EPS ~$15-16 for 2027 and ~$20 run-rate into 2028; x86 share gains continue (client 30.3%, server revenue ~46% of Xeon SP+EPYC). bull.story: MI450/MI500 become a true second source at scale (6GW OpenAI + 6GW Meta + 2GW Anthropic converting on schedule), 2027 EPS beats toward the $20 Street high, premium multiple (~35-40x) sustained as AI TAM narrative ($1.4T accelerator TAM by 2030) holds.

thesis_break_reason: ~34% below today and below the April-August breakout base. Trading there would most likely mean the 2027 'data center more than doubles' plan is broken: a material Helios/MI450 ramp delay (revenue pushed into 2028), a major gigawatt customer (OpenAI/Meta/Anthropic) cutting commitments, or a hyperscaler capex reset, rather than ordinary 72%-vol noise. It would also reprice 2027 EPS toward ~$12 at ~30x.

reasoning: Anchor: $604 close, +281% in a year, ~$1.0T cap, 72% realized vol. Fundamentals are strong and verifiable: Q2 revenue $11.5B (+50%), DC +107%, Q3 guide $13B, non-GAAP GM 56%, management guiding DC to more than double in 2027. Alternative-lane evidence mostly corroborates the demand story but flags execution: Mercury Research (confirmed via Techmeme/PCMag, HotHardware and an X post) shows record x86 share (client 30.3%, total 34.1%), a steady CPU tailwind; Korea Herald/Moor Insights/Tech Insider report Helios in production with customer racks from late Q3 2026; TrendForce prices Helios at $5-5.5M/rack; independent Substacks (EnerTuition) are very bullish and debunked earlier MI450 delay rumours, while SemiAnalysis (Jul 2026) upgraded AMD's odds but warned of a slow rack ramp, internal GPU-cluster shortages and incomplete distributed-inference software, and reported aggressive deal discounts. No liquid prediction market on AMD was found. Valuation: consensus 2027 EPS $15.74 implies ~38x; my blended fair value ~$582 (30x ~$20 2028E, 10x NTM sales) sits ~4% below spot, and the sell-side mean target $618.5 (range $365-$1,250) is near spot too, so I centre the 12-month median at ~$600 (roughly flat) with a slight positive mean. For spread I use a mixture: 80% lognormal sigma 0.50 (forward vol below the 72% realized, as the stock is now a $1T name) and 20% sigma 0.85 for regime tails (Helios failure / AI capex bust, or AI mania continuation). Scenario check: bear $330 (25%), base $610 (50%), bull $950 (25%) -> mean ~$626, consistent with the ladder (P>=604 ~0.50, P>=906 ~0.23, P>=362 ~0.82). Research was focused (~15 queries); some Substack posts are paywalled and X was only reachable via search snippets.
